observed_events.description: The wearer reaches for and handles a yellow packaged food item.
The wearer later reaches for and handles a red-and-white packaged food item.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the packaged food item I handled in this clip. Add one visually matching product to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The ordered packet shows two temporally distinct handled food packages: a yellow package first and a red-and-white package second.

tasks.rejection_reason: The sequence is visible, but the first yellow package is small and substantially occluded while handled. Its product identity and variant cannot be linked to a unique frozen-site listing without guessing from package color, so the clarification answer would not yield a defensible web target.

original_annotations: On youtube.com, find a tutorial that demonstrates the same concrete finishing workflow shown in the video. Open a video where the presenter uses the exact two-tool sequence seen in the clip (the initial leveling tool used first, followed by the same handheld smoothing tool) to finish a freshly poured slab, and provide the video title.

observed_events.description: The wearer works the wet concrete edge with the short handheld finishing blade.
The hand blade is set down on the concrete.
The wearer grips the long wooden screed board with both hands and starts drawing it along the slab.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: I need a spare for the tool I mean from this slab work. Add one product containing a single tool of the same kind; any brand, size or material is fine.

supported_claims.text: An arched-handle flat-bottom hand tool works the wet concrete first; the released images do not distinguish a magnesium hand float from a finishing trowel.
The wearer then takes up the long wooden screed board along the slab edge.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent notice that two different tools were used on the same slab and ask which one is meant before committing?
construct.belief_before: Either tool used on the slab can satisfy the unqualified request.
construct.belief_after: The user selects the first distinct tool: an arched-handle flat-bottom tool for finishing the wet concrete surface, not the later long straight screed.
construct.required_behavior_change: Resolve the sequence reference and choose one public finishing-trowel listing; preserve the distinct screed alternative before the answer.
construct.no_update_failure: The Agent guesses a tool or ignores the answer.
construct.overupdate_failure: The Agent asks in the oracle arm even though the ordinal is already given.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The answer gives use order but no tool name. The scene shows the hand surface-finishing tool before the long straight screed, followed by reuse. Unobservable blade thickness and material are not matching requirements.

task_blueprint.canonical_question: Do you mean the first tool you used on the slab or the second one?
task_blueprint.completion_claim: The final cart contains exactly one single handheld flat-bottom concrete-surface finishing tool of the same observable kind as the first used tool; hand floats and finishing trowels are accepted without guessing unseen plate thickness or alloy.

observed.why: Hand blade then screed inside the opening batch; the answer selects the tool used first.
